Basically, the Kent with her now is Kent’s soul...
It was weird, but not that he hated it.
The Primordial Spirit is Zaila’s soul and mind.
If she were to die now, Zaila would go with her.
They are the same entity, so spending time with their man wasn’t too bad.
Looking at the two ladies’ pleasure him, he couldn’t help but wonder what would be happening to his body on the outside.
But he didn’t think too much about that.
"I have left a mark on your mind, husband.
You can come visit me anytime you want," Zaila’s Primordial Spirit said, making the real Zaila look at her curiously.

"You do know I need you to comprehend all the skills and techniques we acquired, right?" Zaila didn’t want to say it, but her Primordial Spirit had just made arrangements to have free time with Kent behind her back.
"What are you shouting about?
You will feel everything I feel, so don’t get angry."
"You..." Zaila pointed at her Primordial Spirit.
"You sneaky little bitch.
Stay away from my husband."
"You mean our husband.
I am your mind and soul, remember?" the Primordial Spirit said, causing Zaila to stare at her for a few seconds before she sighed.
"You are right, we are indeed the same.
It’s just that even after 2,000 years, I still don’t feel like this is real.
I guess I am just jealous of you because you are more beautiful than I."
She had come to terms with herself, so speaking her feelings wasn’t weird.
Though one would say if she had come to terms with her feelings and made peace with herself, why then become jealous of herself?
The answer is simple: they are women.
You will never understand them.
"Don’t worry, Gaia.
I have a feeling after I give you your True Name, you will look just like her, and perhaps that will be when you fully accept this part of you too.
Know that she is not your clone but you in a spirit form, you are the same entity.
Plus, you should probably give her a name," Kent said.
Zaila nodded at his words, knowing what he said was indeed spot on.
"I guess you are right, Kent.
However, she said she doesn’t need a name, that she will get her name after I get my True Name."
"Oh, why is that?" Kent grew curious, knowing something good was about to happen.
"That’s because she believes I...
I mean, we are reincarnations of someone.
We consulted Big Sister, and she said that because we have this book, we are perhaps related to some old ancient Mind Cultivator known as the Serpent Queen."
The Serpent Manual appeared before them.
"Oh really?
I guess she might be telling the truth.
Though I can’t really understand or say for certain yet, I have my suspicions," Kent said.
"If that is the case, then I guess I should find a way to help your sisters also awaken their Primordial Spirits."
Zaila and her Primordial Spirit stared at each other and giggled.
"We already have a way, but it will take them between 15 to 30 years.
Of course, that time is for you, but to them, they will be gone for thousands of years.
Unlike me, they have True Names, so the only thing left would be to awaken them.
However, to do that, they must first comprehend their Nature.
I can’t explain it, but I know the moment they enter the Primordial Chamber—and yes, that is how we are calling it now—they will find a way to do that and awaken it.
But they can last as long as 30,000 years in there," Zaila said, and Kent nodded with understanding.
"I suppose they’ve already made up their mind, huh?" Kent asked, and Zaila nodded.
"They just want to finish some stuff first before getting back to training."
"I see.
I guess this is good for them.
However, they must first test their combat power, so we will start the mission first.
Then, when they have had enough of that, they can enter the Primordial Chamber."
"I also have to enter seclusion for a few hundred years myself."
Kent said.
The time difference really is something that’s coming in handy—not only for me, but for the humans living in the city.
They’re all making progress thanks to the passing of time, which isn’t affecting their age.
They were aging based on the time outside, so even though nearly two years had passed since they arrived in the tower, only a month had passed in the outside world.
Kent talked about a few things with Zaila and her Primordial Spirit before he and Zaila left.
"That was wild," Kent said, looking at Zaila, who had just broken their kiss-the kiss that had sent them into the Mind Space.
"This is a cultivation world; things like this happen all the time," Zaila responded with a small smile.
"I guess you’re right.
I must hurry and awaken your True Name quickly and see what will happen," Kent said.
"I look forward to it.
For now, I want more of your yang essence.
I want it all over my face."
Just like that, another intense session started—one in which Kent released his cum many times, painting her face in creamy juice and satisfying Zaila’s fantasy.
"Are you happy now?" Kent asked, watching Zaila now bathed in his cum.
The facial she wanted had been fulfilled.
She scooped a finger full of cum and licked it, making sure her tongue came out seductively.
"This is the best time of my life.
I’ll come for more later.
For now, bye."
Zaila smiled and vanished, appearing in front of the Yin Pool.
When her sisters saw her messy look, they all gulped.
"That’s it.
We are all getting facials," Vexthra said, and her sisters seconded.
Thus, they scooped their share of the cum and walked back into the pool.
The only ones who didn’t do anything were Lady Vari, Elaine, and Velyra, who didn’t know how to feel about all this.

chapters.title: Chapter 554: The Bloodmancer [Bonus]
paragraphs: After Zaila left, Kent turned to the message he had received when he made Zaila his 12th wife.
The Soul Essence he received was through the roof, and while he didn’t know it, there was something called Mental Points. When he received it, his mind expanded by several degrees.
All of this was something Zaila gave him. However, the most unique of them all was the gift he received in the form of a manual.
When he added Val, he received a realm comprehension tablet that would allow him and his wives to comprehend their realms easily.
However, now, it was a manual.
"This reminds me of the perfect Alchemist manual I neglected to read. This time, I will read this," Kent said, taking out a blood-red manual with only a few pages.
"Legend of the Bloodmancer," Kent muttered, reading the name on the book. However, before he could open it, a purple spell circle appeared on it, making it impossible to open.
Currently seated on her throne inside the Nameless Temple, the Enchantress shook in her seat. She quickly formed a series of hand seals and then drew a line.
The line appeared surrounded by 13 growing orbs. After observing it for a few minutes, she sighed. However, a frown appeared on her face.
"Don’t look at me. I didn’t send that to him." Suddenly, the voice of the lady sitting at the core of the universe entered her ears.
"If you didn’t, then who?" the Enchantress asked.
"I was wondering if you have the answer." The Enchantress shook her head.
"The timeline is still the same. Nobody tampered with it, and from what I know about the Universe Pool, it wouldn’t give that manual to him just yet. So what is happening?"
"I think we should prevent him from reading it," the lady at the core said, but the Enchantress shook her head.
"There has to be a reason why he received the book now. If anything, we should be prepared instead for the outcome.
He who never appeared in the history books cannot be ignored now either.
If he was meant to exist, the least we can do is ensure he isn’t consumed by it."
The two ladies came to an agreement, and Kent, who had been trying various methods to open the book, suddenly succeeded. The pages were dark, and the words were written in red.
"What a weird book," Kent said, but he couldn’t help himself. He started reading, not noticing a red symbol forming on his forehead the moment he read the first line.

"The path of the Bloodmancer is one shrouded in mystery, blood, and the deepest of forbidden arts. Those who tread this path possess the power to manipulate the very essence of life—blood, using it as both a weapon and a tool of unimaginable power.
Bloodmancers can bend the blood of others to their will, create devastating attacks, and even control life and death itself.
However, they were never recorded because bloodmancy was a forbidden art that had been forgotten by all.
The first Bloodmancer—the one who created the first Bloodfiend—was never recorded in the history books, for his life wasn’t considered viable enough to be remembered.
However, the legends of the fallen, those who were forgotten, once spoke of the legendary Bloodmancer—one said to possess supreme authority over blood.
His story began as a young boy who lost everything before he was even born. His birth came from a dead soldier, whose flickering life force kept him alive until he was born.
His life was horrible from the start.
When the Blood Emperor’s men found him, he was just a baby crying in the mud of blood, with no energy or knowledge to move forward.
They took him in and catered to him. Slowly, he started to grow. He became a teenager who, after many tries, still couldn’t cultivate, so they made him a worker in a plantation.
Years later, when he was 20 and the first wall of the Breaking Shadows arrived, the Blood Race had to join the battle. That year, the Blood Emperor died, and his race was nearly driven to extinction.
Varek was left with nowhere to go. So, when the second battle arrived three years after the first, his life came to an end.
He ran for his life, but he could only get so far.
However, legend speaks of his near-death. They said that when he was on the verge of death, the timeline was split into two, and Varek found himself in the middle.
Nobody knew why the timeline split, but legend spoke of the moment the 14 legions came from the future to the pass heeding their masters call.
He was stuck between dying timeline and a probable one.
The forgotten legend spoke of the moment Varek witnessed the bloodcurdling battle that shouldn’t have happened. He saw the 14 legions arrive in their elegance.
He witnessed the moment the last piece of Chaos’s dragon soul left and entered the channels of time and space, traveling to both the future and the past.

He saw creatures of the unknown—creatures that should neither be seen nor remembered. However, Varek witnessed them all, and the moment everything ended, he found himself back in his own body, but as a child.
That was the day he rose from weakness, awakening his first Bloodheart. Legend has it that when he formed his first Bloodheart, his name was changed from Varek to Dracula, the first Bloodmancer.
"Chills," Kent muttered, reading the last page. He felt his soul smile briefly when he finished reading the book.
"Varek... Dracula. I never knew the legend of Dracula was completely different, and from how it was written, this person was much more of a forbidden-born."
Kent surprisingly made sense of everything, and for some strange reason, he had the urge to read more of this account.
However, he only had the first part. He stored the book away and sighed. Then, a sudden realization made him snap his eyes open.
"This may be a coincidence, but Bloodheart and Bloodheart Stone must be the same thing, right?" Kent suddenly felt a conspiracy building up.
"That can’t be it, right?" he wondered. However, he knew he would have to wait until he got his hands on this Bloodheart Stone.
"Things are getting interesting," Kent said, looking forward to the future.
The Enchantress and the Mother Uninverse smile watching the brat put away the book.

chapters.title: Chapter 555: Meeting the Members of The Eternal Wrath (1) [Bonus]
paragraphs: Kent spent a few hours resting. When he had had enough rest, he dressed up and went to meet his legion.
Kaizo and his team were back from their last dungeon runs, so when they returned, all of them, along with some new faces, were training inside the legion tower.
However, not all of them were training outside. There were eight portals leading to eight dungeons, so some had entered and were battling monsters there instead.
His main undead legion was present, and the new faces were the eight dungeon bosses he had added to his legion.
When he appeared, Kaizo was the first to notice him.
"Master, are we going on another mission?" he asked, making everyone aware their master had arrived. They immediately stopped all they were doing and surrounded him.
"There is something different about you," Sylara, the one-eyed demoness, said, sniffing Kent. Aside from the obvious scent of his having had sex with his wife, Sylara seemed to sense something else.
"Your blood... it has become more powerful, and from the smell, very sweet. I would like a taste, Master," she said, and Kent could only shake his head.
"Why not?" He gave her his arm, and Sylara wasted no time taking a bite. When the first drop of blood entered her mouth, her body shuddered, releasing a powerful energy.
She dragged a mouthful of blood before letting go of his arm.
Kent looked at where she bit, and to his surprise, it had healed up.
"Your blood—it’s both sweet, full of energy, and there’s something else about it I just can’t understand," Sylara said, savoring the bite.
"I recently comprehended Chaos energy, so I think that’s the other thing."
His legion stood there staring at him. The way he said it casually made them wonder if he knew what this meant. However, the clueless Kaizo didn’t let them ponder it further.
"Master is awesome, we all know that. However, are we going on a new mission?" he asked, and Kent shook his head.
"We will go on the mission soon. I just came to check up on our new guests," Kent said, staring at the eight dungeon bosses.
"You guys are powerful. Care to introduce yourselves?" Kent asked. "By the way, I am Kent Madson, the one who summoned all eight of you."
"Master, there is something you should know first," Kaizo said, looking at the eight.
"What?"
"I don’t think they have their memories. Well, they are getting fragments, but aside from their names, they don’t have much recollection of their past."
"Oh, I see," Kent was surprised to hear that. Though he expected such a possibility, he never thought it would be true.
"Then your names, and if you remember something small about yourself, will be enough for now. Though it is not compulsory to know anything," Kent said.
The orc chieftain was the first to speak.
"I am Skoggr, chieftain of the Bloodmourn Clan. I don’t know how I am here, but I remember being the chieftain of this tribe for many years."
Kent nodded. "It was nice meeting you, Skoggr. Don’t worry; I will help you regain your memories."
The orc nodded. The next in line, the demi-human wyvern, introduced himself.
"I am Kha’azal, once a guardian of the sacred Tempest Peak."
⟪I know that place. It is in the Nine Immortal Worlds. There are three of them: the Tempest Peak, the Flame Peak, and the Radiance Peak.
The Tempest is the strongest of the three.
The tempest peak was the holy grounds of the Wyvern race and the only thing keeping the dragons from invading their lands and taking control of their race.
If he is or was indeed a guardian there, then you have yourself a powerful warrior. Also, looking at his true realm, I think he’s not lying,⟫ Dori suddenly spoke, making Kent widen his eyes slightly.
"Guardian of the Sacred Tempest Peak. Looks like you’re a big shot, huh?" Kent said, and Kha’azal looked at him curiously.
"Do you know that place?" he asked.
"No, however, I have a subordinate who does. She’s busy now, but when she’s free, she’ll come so you can have a chat with her. Just know that you’re a big shot."
Kha’azal smiled.
"What about me?" Skoggr asked, and Kent smiled, shaking his head.
"Don’t look down, Skoggr. After taking care of business here, we’ll be going to the higher worlds soon. We’ll surely come across your tribe or your kind soon enough."
The orc chieftain nodded.
Kent used his Enchanted Eyes to scan them and see if what Dori said was true. After what happened with Velyra, scanning people wasn’t something he did instinctively anymore.
⟦Name: Skoggr DruBoggr⟧
⟦Title: The Bloodmourn⟧
⟦Role: Chieftain⟧
⟦Current Realm: Root Sovereign (Peak)⟧
⟦True Realm: Spirit Immortal (Two Immortal Auras)⟧
⟦Name: Kha’azal Drogan⟧
⟦Title: The Stormbringer ⟧
⟦Role: Guardian of the Tempest Peak⟧
⟦Current Realm: Root Sovereign (Peak)⟧
⟦True Realm: True Immortal (Four Immortal Auras)⟧
’Damn, they are impressive,’ Kent said inwardly, reading their status pages.
⟪Looks like the limitations of the medium worlds are affecting them.
However, the moment they enter a high world, they will gradually recover to their peak, and the same will happen when they reach an immortal world.
Still, I advise you to take your alchemy seriously, Master.

Though they are immortals, their bodies will need time to adapt and fully restore their strength in higher worlds. But with body tempering now, and by making more pills for them, they can recover much faster to aid you when you need them⟫, Dori said, and Kent nodded inwardly.
He turned to the third dungeon boss, the skull-headed man known as the Shade King.
"I am Nykali. I don’t have any recollection aside from my name," Nykali said with a sigh. Kent patted him on the shoulder and smiled.
"Don’t worry, we all have memories locked away. One day we’ll remember them, and when that time comes, we can return to where we’re supposed to be."
Though his head was a skull and he looked terrifying, his true realm was that of an Immortal King—someone several times stronger than even Kha’azal.

chapters.title: Chapter 556: Meeting the Members of The Eternal Wrath (2) [Bonus]
paragraphs: Kent’s eyes landed on the fourth dungeon boss, who, despite undergoing training inside the Dead Region, knew at a glance that a battle with the flame brute wielding the hammer wouldn’t end well for him.

⟪I know you can sense it, master, and no, you can’t measure up to him, strength-wise. This person is made from the remnant of a dying star, one of the seven fallen bodies. You don’t need to know what these fallen bodies are just yet.

However, the person before you is made of one of the fallen bodies known as the Flameheart. His flame is the essence of a star—someone you can’t handle easily, despite having chaos qi running through you.
However, battling him will be good for you since it will temper your body and make you more flame-resistant.
And before you ask, his comprehension of the flame element is already at the Perfect stage, even for an Immortal King.⟫
’Damn, why are my subordinates more impressive than me?’ Kent said inwardly, hearing Dori speak about the flame brute speak.
His true height is 12 feet; however, he maintained 10 feet during the battle with the hunter, and now, he is 7 feet.
But despite the reduction in height, he is still intimidating.
"I am Aetheris. I also don’t have any recollections yet, but I know I am impressive by all standards."
"That’s the arrogance I’m talking about. Just because he’s stronger than all of us doesn’t mean you have to rub it in our faces, okay?" Kaizo glared at the brute, who smirked.
His body is made of molten lava, but no heat is coming from him. This is because his control of flame is at the Perfect stage, allowing him perfect control over it.
"Don’t worry, Kaizo. He can be arrogant for now. When he meets that lady, I’m sure he’ll shut up." Zareth, who caused Kaizo’s trauma when they faced Aetheris, consoled him.
Kent just laughed, knowing he must get to know what happened inside the dungeon since he wasn’t with them.
Next was the lion-headed beast-man, who, from the looks of things, seemed to prefer being quiet. He stood there silently, not saying anything until Kent looked at him.
"I am Ka’zarak."
That was all he said. However, Kent didn’t mind scanning the rest. It turns out he is much more impressive.
His nature is that of a warden of beasts, just like the third Night Rider Kent had undercover inside the Dark Devil Church.
However, there is a twist to his powers. Instead of summoning the beasts, they summon him instead and engage in combat with him.
If he wins, they become his subordinates. However, he can’t be summoned now; those he is contracted to are also dormant.
However, he can summon five beasts from the dungeon he commands.
"Nice having you on the team, Ka’zarak," the lion-headed man nodded.
"I am Veera, a necromancer," the sixth dungeon boss introduced herself, causing Kent to look around.
"If you’re looking for that lady, she’s inside that cocoon," Kaizo pointed in the direction of a large, dark cocoon. The hunter he had taken as his servant was still undergoing her transformation.
"So I have three necromancers on my side now, huh? I wonder which one of you is more impressive," Kent said, causing Veera to turn and look at Nykali, the bone-headed dungeon boss.
Nykali isn’t exactly a necromancer; however, since he summons spectral beings, he can be considered one. Veera, on the other hand, can be dubbed both a warrior and a necromancer.
Both she and Ka’zarak are True Immortals. However, because of the suppression of the medium world, they have regressed to Peak Sovereigns, though their true realms still await recovery.
The seventh is also an orc. However, he is also a barbarian, making him even stronger than Skoggr. Kent looked at him and knew Kaizo would become his best friend.
"I am Gorzak, the Barbarian King."
⟪The barbarian race—one of the best body cultivators in the universe. No wonder he’s already a Diamond Body at his current cultivation level. You should exchange blows with him, master.
Make it a pure brute battle, where no skills aside from raw muscle strength will be used.⟫ Dori said with a giggle.
’I will do just that,’ Kent smiled.
Then comes the assassin. He is a slender man with the perfect human form, except for his eyes, which are like those of a panther. However, everything else about him is human.
During the fight with the hunter’s abominations, he morphed into a partial panther form, taking his strength to the next level. Now, he is a simple human dressed in black.
"Valtor," he said, simply stating his name, showing how secretive he is as an assassin.
Both he and the Barbarian King, Gorzak, are True Immortals. Kent smiled happily, knowing his legion kept rising with the passing of the days.
"This is your home now. I will, however, find a way to uncover your true backgrounds and help recover your memories. But for now, feel free to live your best lives here.
If you need anything, just say the word, and it will be provided."
All eight of them nodded.
"Master, when can we go on a mission?" Kaizo asked. But Kent grabbed his ear and pulled him closer to whisper.
"I’ll give you a new mission—if you can defeat Gorzak." Kent had noticed Kaizo didn’t like the guy, so he wanted to keep him quiet for a few days.
However, he was shocked when Kaizo lunged at the guy, and just like that, the two brutes engaged in fierce combat.
"Don’t mind them," Kent laughed, watching the display. "I will bring over the last four dungeons."
"Nice one. I can’t wait to meet that hateful lady again. Also, I think she has a crush on Veydris," Sylara said, getting herself ready for battle.
"Wait, Veydris has a girlfriend? This is interesting." Kent turned and looked at his emotionless knight, who had emerged from his metal armor and was now clad in sleek metal and leather armor.
His height had also reduced, and surprisingly, he looked adorable.
"Veydris was the one who defeated her. But I think she let him win. I’m not sure, however, one thing is certain—she’s a psycho," Sylara said, clearly not liking the mysterious lady.
Kent laughed and asked, "If she’s a psycho, what does that make you?"
His laughter rang out as he bound the four dungeons to the tower, making four more portals appear beside the existing eight.

chapters.title: Chapter 557: Irina, Veydris Crush [Bonus]
paragraphs: The moment the portals formed, Kent summoned the last four dungeon bosses. Just like the previous eight, the new arrivals were all at the peak of the Sovereign stage.
However, their true realms were much more impressive.
That was especially true for the lady who, despite standing before Kent, had a presence that was nearly non-existent. It was as if she wasn’t there at all.
"That’s her, Master. She is the strongest of all twelve," Zareth said, looking in the direction of the lady who was smiling at Veydris.
Naturally, the metal knight stood there emotionless. Whatever the lady was selling, Veydris wasn’t buying it.
Seeing they were looking at her, she turned and introduced herself.

"I am Irina. You can also call me the Veil of Shadows. I have control over shadow and the void," she said with a smile. Though she was neither an elf nor a dark elf, her ears were much longer than the average human’s.
However, she was clearly human in appearance.
"How strong is your control over the Void?" Kent asked.
"I have perfect control," she answered, making Kent widen his eyes.
"Do you think you can help Veydris improve his control? His level is at the Very High level." For a moment, Kent could swear Veydris glared at him.
Clearly, the metal knight didn’t like the arrangement his master had made for him. Irina, however, was ecstatic to get to spend time with Veydris.
"I will do my best to teach him," she said, almost jumping with joy.
"Master, why did you let this hateful lady get close to Veydris? You know he doesn’t like to be disturbed, right?" Sylara whispered, making sure Veydris didn’t hear.
"I want him to improve. Maybe that will make him start to talk," Kent said, but Sylara, ever the big sister, glared at Irina.
"If you mess with him, we’ll have an issue—and trust me, you don’t want to have an issue with me. Isn’t that right, Zareth, Vaelros?" Sylara had to call two lawyers.
"Sylara is right. Don’t mess with Veydris."
Kent wondered if he should tell them that the lady they were messing with was only a step away from becoming a demigod.
Irina’s true realm was Immortal Monarch—someone at the peak of the immortal realm. So for three beings not even at the Core Formation stage to be messing with her...
Kent just laughed, watching the display. While the four were at it, he turned to the next dungeon boss—a dragon man.
He had a handsome human face and dragon horns. Strangely, one of his horns was broken in half, and a dark mark was on his left cheek.
"Zhar’kaz, the Flamewing Tyrant. Also, I think I was a general of an army of some kind," the dragon man said.
"A general, huh. Do you remember which unit you commanded?" Kent asked, but he shook his head.
"I only remember bits and pieces, but I know for sure I was a fearsome general by all standards."
’Ah, that arrogance,’ Kent sighed, knowing that arrogant trait was within him too—as in every dragon out there.
However, he couldn’t deny the bold claims. His true realm was Immortal Emperor, just a step behind Irina.
This made him very dangerous. While his current realm was Sovereign, his control over flame was at the Perfect level.
"I have no doubt you were an impressive general. I hope you remember who you are soon so we can see if your impressiveness was indeed warranted."
The dragon man smiled, hearing what Kent said.
"You are a Demon Lord," Kent said, staring at the third dungeon boss.
"I am. You can call me Vorthar, the Warbringer."
"I do not doubt that, for I know what Demon Lords can do," Kent said with a smile.

From Jest’s memories, he knew who the Demon Lords were and the role they played in the demon race. They were directly beneath the Demon Kings, who were beneath the Demon Emperor, who was in turn beneath the Demon Monarch.
However, despite being ranked beneath the Demon Kings, Demon Lords were some of the most dangerous demons one could ever encounter.
When Jest went on his journey to see if he could find a path higher than the Sword King stage, he nearly died by the sword of a Demon Lord.
So, seeing one now, Kent didn’t know if he should feel happy or haunted by that traumatizing experience.
"Are demons really immune to injuries?" Kent asked a different question instead. He didn’t want to think about that painful memory anymore.
"We indeed have powerful regeneration abilities. However, we are not immune," Vorthar answered, and Kent nodded.
Vorthar was a True Immortal, just like most of the dungeon bosses.
"In any case, welcome to the team." Kent turned to the last of them. This one, however, was beauty by all standards.
She had a regal, coldly beautiful face with pale blue eyes. Her face was smooth and sharp, with high cheekbones and full lips, giving her an almost ethereal beauty.
Her hair was long, flowing, and pure white, with strands of glistening frost that sparkled like diamonds.
She was slender and tall, standing around seven feet. Her body was graceful but unnaturally still, like a perfect ice sculpture.
She wore an elegant gown made of enchanted ice crystals, which constantly shimmered with blue and white light. Her arms were covered in delicate, ice-formed gauntlets.
The ground she stood on was frozen around her, radiating an intense cold.
⟪Beautiful, cold, and elegant. I wonder what an Elemental is doing inside a dungeon⟫, Gaia said, making Kent wonder the same thing.
"You are an Elemental, right?" Kent asked, and the lady nodded.
"My name is Ankaara. I am an Ice Elemental from the Absolute White Crystal Race. And if you’re wondering what an Elemental is doing inside a dungeon, the answer is simple:
"My family banished me. However, I didn’t die like they intended—meaning I will have my revenge."
⟪An Ice Elemental, hellbent on revenge. Looks like you’ll be having some chilling trouble on your hands, Master⟫. The three lolis laughed, making Kent smirk.
"Do you want to talk about it?" Kent asked, and Ankaara nodded.

chapters.title: Chapter 558: Ankaara, The Ice Elemental Princess [Bonus]
paragraphs: The 12 dungeon bosses were not supposed to have their memories. At best, they were supposed to have bits and pieces. However, the Ice Princess, who was the last to introduce herself, still has her memories.
This was a shock to the 11 dungeon bosses and even Kent himself.
Kent didn’t know why she still had her memories, but he could speculate that she had been in the dungeon for only a few years compared to the rest.
Perhaps that was the case, but he wasn’t too concerned about that, considering his main focus now was learning about Ankaara and why she wanted revenge on her family.
"First of all, I still have every last bit and piece of my memories. My full name is Ankaara Frostveil, of the royal family of the White Crystal Elemental race.
I am next in line to the throne of our race in the 67 Continental World. My mother was the Queen Mother, and my father is the King.
However, when my mother died, things changed. My stepmother, using her bewitching powers, corrupted my father to the point that he declared my junior sister the next Crown Queen.
Not that I minded. I never wanted the responsibility of being queen anyway. However, while I didn’t, my sister and her mother wanted it so badly that my presence became a headache to them.

So they went further and, for hundreds of years, did all they could to ruin my name. When they couldn’t, they conspired with the Flame Void Elemental race, one of the powerhouses in the 67 Continental Worlds.

They wanted to marry me off to some no-name, useless, incredibly substandard, stupid prince of that race. I refused, and while this marriage would indeed have brought our two races together, my refusal wasn’t taken lightly.
But I am a princess, and nobody can force me. But what I failed to notice was the extent to which my stepmother and her daughter would go.

After being asked seven times, it turns out my refusal went against an old rule of my race I wasn’t aware of, and the punishment for that was banishment into the Void Region—a place from which no one who traverses it has ever returned.
It was between marrying that ugly bastard or death. However, I didn’t hesitate to choose death. My soul and spirit wouldn’t accept that marriage, so I chose death.
However, when I was banished into the Void and at death’s door, I was miraculously teleported into the dungeon as the last floor boss. I’ve been there for 590 years already.

I have my memories—every last one of them—and as for my realm, I know my true cultivation is at the Immortal Emperor stage, just a step away from becoming an Immortal Monarch. Then I can start comprehending divinity to become a demigod."
By the time Ankaara finished her narrative, the only ones not seething were Kaizo and Gorzak, the Barbarian King, who were still clashing in fierce combat.
Well, Veydris couldn’t be angry either, so there were three of them. The rest could sense Ankaara’s anger and knew she meant it when she said she would get her revenge.
However, Irina asked a question that made Kent look at Ankaara after glaring at the shadow lady.

"Sounds to me like you managed to get your life back. I mean, you didn’t want to marry that scum nor become the queen. Also, your mother died, and as for your dad, he’s a loser who couldn’t control his dick. So now that you’re here with us, I think you’re safe... right?"
Ankaara wasn’t angry about Irina’s words. It felt like she needed to hear that. She even smiled upon hearing her harsh words.

"You’re right, Irina. My life has indeed turned out well. However, the reason I want revenge isn’t for me, but for my mother. She died, but I didn’t say how she died, until the last moments of my life"
"Let me guess, those losers poisoned her," Vorthar, the Demon Lord, said.
"They did more than that. They stole her Soul Root and Elemental Core. And let me tell you, losing even one of those is more painful than anything you can ever imagine.

I only found out the day before I was banished. My mother was a genius among immortals. She was the best. However, they went ahead and did something that grim to her—all so they could make that bitch called my sister a genius too."
"These bastards want to die so badly," Aetheris, the brute born from the fallen body, said, radiating killing qi.
The others weren’t far behind.
"Let’s all calm down now, guys. The current us can’t do much. However, that doesn’t mean we won’t do anything." Kent turned toward Ankaara.

He studied her expression first. "I don’t know where your world is, but I do know we’ll get there one day. I have faith we’ll get there, and when we do, trust me, we’ll rain fury on them—and if possible, make their descendants pay for their crimes."
Kent spoke those words naturally, in a calming way, but to those hearing him, they sensed words full of determination and anger—ones that screamed for justice.
"For now, make yourself at home. These are all your brothers and sisters. We are one big family, and we will only grow in the future, so get acquainted with them.
If you need anything, just ask and it will be provided. There is an entire world to explore here and out there, so get used to your new life."
Ankaara nodded, hearing Kent’s words.
Kent went to examine the cocoon where Yi Lai, the hunter, was undergoing her transformation for a few minutes.
After a while, he left and went back to the Mountain Garden, where the three lolis seemed to have figured out something and wanted to talk to him about it.
He may have only heard about Ankaara’s life, but something told him he wasn’t the only one with such a tragic backstory.
He had a feeling the others also shared the same setting, and thus, he knew what had to be done—but for now, he would let time handle things.

"You are already a goddess," Lilian, her best friend, said, smiling.
The two had already planned to share the same man even before Kent entered the scene, so they were practically living their dreams.
Lady Vari, Elaine, and Velyra were paying close attention to what the sisters were talking about.
Neomi, who said this, moved closer to Velyra and decided to quench her curiosity.
The moment she told her what she needed to know, she moved back to allow her to digest what she heard.
A couple of hours later, Lady Lani and Nara returned with facials, causing their sisters to do as they had with Zaila.
Their two new sisters were also wielding the same shamelessness as the rest of their sisters.
Of course, this made them happy because they knew that shyness would be eliminated in their future moments with their man.
Kent left and went back to the mountain garden to relax and examine what he had received from the Universe this time around.

chapters.title: Chapter 564: City of Angels
paragraphs: "Destiny Key." Kent retrieved a golden key that looked rather beautiful for a key. He quickly appraised it using his Enchanted Eyes.
"Fascinating... not even a name." Kent turned the key around for a few seconds, even going as far as dripping his blood on it to see if that would trigger something. However, nothing happened.
"No name, no description aside from the obvious name, which for some reason sounded vague." Kent stared hard at the key, but nothing triggered, so he let it rest.
"I don’t know which destiny this key will open, but it feels important even though I don’t know what it does. I’d better hold on to it securely," He put it in his tower storage
Kent sighed, knowing the failure to identify the use of the key wasn’t deliberate. Perhaps the laws didn’t want him to know just yet, or maybe something entirely was blocking him from knowing.
However, while he was sighing, far in the cosmos, perhaps farther from Kent’s universe, a star shone brightly for a few minutes before dimming.
Though he was quick to put the key in his Tower storage, inside that storage, the key also shone for a few more minutes before it calmed down.
Kent relaxed his muscles for a few minutes before he went ahead to check the second item.
This was a manual, just like the one he had received about the first Bloodmancer.
"The City of Angels."
That was the title of the manual. He quickly opened it, and to his surprise, it was written in a language he could read, so he dug in.
"Long ago, before the war of the Angels and demons, marking the destruction of one of the greatest races and the disappearance of another, there was an angel called Seraphil.
She was one of the five daughters of the Angel King.
Despite being the youngest of her sisters, she was regarded as the strongest. This was because she had never put her sword down since the day she learned how to walk.
Many called her a man-woman because she never dressed like a woman. She preferred her trousers and leather long-sleeved regardless of the event she was invited to or required to attend.
This made her unattractive to her sisters and most angel Princes
However, she didn’t care because she had many friends with whom she played daily, despite her family’s constant reminders that she was a princess.

Eventually, thousands of years passed, and Seraphil became a big shot in the Angel army. She even qualified to become the general of the entire army. However, she rejected the offer and said she would rather remain a loyal soldier.
Though that was just bullshit, nobody would dare command someone who could defeat the general with just a single move.
Her family tried to bring her back to the royal family to do her duties as a princess, but she rejected them at every turn.
"I would rather marry my sword than another man." That was her reply every time. Eventually, the royal family forgot they had a fifth daughter, something she wanted.
However, one fateful day, without any warning, the demon army arrived with nothing but murder in their eyes.
It was an impromptu battle that the angel race, despite being known as one of the races wielding the mightiest army in the universe, was caught off guard.
The battle was severe and brutal; however, half the angel army was annihilated when it ended. Their general was captured and executed the next day after the battle.
His head hung at the crossing.
This angered the angel race, but retaliation wasn’t an option with their army cut in half. This broke Seraphil’s heart.
She wanted revenge, but she was not allowed, even going as far as locking her in the most secure prison in fear she might poison her fellow soldiers into following her to their unfortunate death.

But while they thought they were protecting her and her fellow soldiers, what they never planned was the fact that locking her in the most secure prison of the angel race would bring her closer to Bob, a mysterious prisoner who had been locked there for millions of years.
She met Bob, who, after ten years, found out was a swordsman with an unrivaled technique that once shook the universe.
"Starfall"
When Seraphil found out Bob was the creator of the infamous Starfall sword technique, she tried everything she could to make him teach her.
However, no matter what she did, Bob was never moved. Thus, the last hundred years of Seraphil’s life before she was released were spent hating Bob for being selfish.

She knew if she learned Starfall, she alone could get the revenge she craved on the demon race. But alas, Bob never even flinched when she asked, even going as far as offering to marry him and become his wife.
Bob’s existence was strange and unique.
After her release, she tried to discover more about him, but nobody knew anything about his lineage, not even the Angel King.
However, she did find something: Bob was the mysterious swordsman who defeated a clone of Lord Genesis a long time ago.
However, was he really the same person? Was Bob the person who defeated a clone of the father of swordsmen?
Was he truly the creator of Starfall?
If he were indeed the creator, then what is Starfall? What exactly is Starfall?
Something that made a princess who hated the word marriage offer to marry Bob just for the technique named Starfall.
If that was the case, what then happened to Bob after the Angel race disappeared? Was he perhaps taken with them since the prison is part of the Angel race domain?
If he died, does that mean the legendary technique died with him?
Also, what happened to Seraphil?
One more thing, who exactly is Bob?
Many questions remain unanswered, including the legend of the City of Angels, the brave warrior princess, and Bob.
Perhaps this is just a big giant coincidence, but then again, are coincidences really a thing?"
Kent took a deep sigh, closing the book.
"City of Angels"
"Seraphil"
"Bob"
"Starfall"
Kent placed the four names in the back of his mind. He knew things were not as simple as they appeared, so those four names stayed in his thoughts.
Thus, he knew he must look into it. However, he had other engagements to attend to first.

chapters.title: Chapter 565: True Name Awakening, Three New Wives [Bonus]
paragraphs: "Ladies, put some clothes on," Kent said to his ladies as he arrived in the love garden.
They glared at him, clearly not wanting to do that.
"...I want to awaken your true names, so go put some clothes on before you all seduce me... especially you, big sister Vari. I like your ass by the way, you too Elaine and my redskin beauty."
The Kingdom Protector’s and her two new best friends’ cheeks turned beet red when Kent said that. In fact, she never wanted to look him in the eye ever again. Kent was just too shameless.
Thankfully, she had some easy-to-wear clothes on hand, so she covered her body as everyone before Kent sent them to the Soul Tower.
Elaine and Velyra did the same thing.
So far, Kent had awakened Lilian, Elsa, Ingrid, Selene, Nara, and Neomi’s True Names.

This means the only ones left are Mara, Camilla, Val, Zaila, Lady Lani, Vexthra, Lady Vari, and Velyra. And yes, Kent wanted to awaken all their true names, regardless of whether he had slept with them or not.
He knew right after he came out of seclusion, it would be missions and exploration, so he wouldn’t be selfish and think that, because he hadn’t slept with them, they shouldn’t have true names.

They were his forever when he brought them to his harem tower. The sex was just to strengthen him. But even now that the tower seemed to have expanded its reach on where he got his strength from, the sex part could wait.
They all had primordial paths they were following, except for Elaine and Velyra, so Kent wanted to push them to the level where they could fight alongside their sisters against powerful enemies.
However, aside from his clear plan to make them have true names, he also wanted to test out something Gaia said.
But aside from them, there are two special cases he can’t deal with now.
He knew Elaine and Unity were special cases. One required a destiny token, and the other must have the curse on her bloodline broken.
So they were the exceptions. But Kent had a plan for them soon, and that would be right after he awakened the soul path Vexthra prepared for him.
"The plan is simple. I will awaken your bloodlines, except for Elaine and Unity, who are special cases. But aside from them, I will awaken your true names, which will make you very powerful.

Afterwards, you will enter the Primordial Chamber and awaken your primordial spirit. For that, Elaine and Unity, you must join, since that will push you to be at the same level as your sisters, even without true names."
"Then, when the last of you comes out from seclusion, we will start the mission. I only hope by then, you all can stand tall and face the danger without fear."
The ladies laughed, clearly happy.
Kent walked closer to the three ladies: Elaine, Lady Vari, and Velyra. "I know you need some time to get used to you being my woman.
So, I will officially make you my woman now, and then when we get to know each other more, we can take it to the next level."
They nodded, even Velyra nodded. She would be lying if she said she didn’t feel something for Kent.
At first, maybe she just wanted to save her people, but after the battle, she felt something for him, and that feeling was later amplified by Vexthra, who knew Kent also liked her.
There are many ladies in the tower, but despite Kent’s playboy personality, he had only spent time with one, Elaine.
This shows he indeed shows interest in the ones he likes. He showed interest in Velyra, and now, she is becoming his wife.
Lady Vari, also surprisingly, agreed to become his woman. Though she had been stubborn from the start, she knew her life had changed after spending months with the ladies.
She now wanted to forever spend her time with the ladies and surprisingly, with the brat who was now being hunted down in every city across the four Kingdoms.
’Gaia, do it.’
Kent gave the order, and the three ladies were added. However, aside from the message that he had added his 15th wife, Lady Vari, 16th, Elaine, and 17th, Velyra, there were no other messages.
However, the tower told him they would come after they got their true names. This meant the condition to get those benefits was either a true name or sex.
Kent nodded to that, and so he retrieved the first true name token.
"I have a question, though," Velyra said, and Kent nodded.
"What happens when I get my true name? More importantly, what is a true name?"

"True names are your true identity. They stand for who you are. They hold your bloodline, your potential, and even your soul. So to possess a true name is to regain control over your true potential, your path, and, more importantly, your identity.
Two people can share the same name, but only one person can possess a true name. Generally, the moment your true name is invoked, your endless potential will be unleashed."
Kent himself didn’t know much about true names, but from what he had seen after awakening the true names of his ladies, he was able to coin the definition of a true name from it.
Thankfully, Velyra managed to grasp the meaning from it.

"Don’t worry, your tribe will be shocked when they see you after your awakening. Trust me, the true names he gives us aren’t the regular ones," Vexthra said to Velyra, who nodded and became quiet. She most definitely wanted to see what would happen.
In fact, Lady Vari and Elaine were just as curious.
As for Zaila, she wanted to see what would become of her primordial spirit after the awakening.
"Mara, you are first to go," Kent said, and Mara stepped forward. She dripped her blood on the token, and Kent did the same.
Right when his blood touched the token, the sky cleared, and one of the 13 moons in the sky came into view. Hanging behind it were two large angel wings, spread wide and exuding potent lunar energy.
"Wow," the ladies widened their eyes, watching as Mara was taken off the ground and lifted into the air before disappearing into the moon.
The wings behind the moon enclosed the moon, shielding it from all eyes.

chapters.title: Chapter 566: Selphira Lunaris [Bonus]
paragraphs: Long after the Angelic Order fell and the Angel race parted, a child was born to the Moonlit Angel race during the alignment of the Celestial Star and the Harmonious Moon.
They called her Seraphina Moonveil, for she was the one born when all hope was lost.

She was born during a rare celestial event—an event that happens once every million years. However, millions of years after the Angelic Order fell, peace was not born again in the remaining Angel race.
Her birth brought hope to her people, and for years, she was nurtured. Her name was used to bring peace to the remaining Angel race.
Her name was used to deter all enemies, and as she grew, her radiance started to manifest. Before she turned 20, she became a symbol that stood at the forefront of the Moonlit Angel race.
Under her authority, the broken and shattered Angel race was made whole again. Under her authority, the Moonlit Order was formed...
Just like that, for thousands of years, using her strength and authority, she brought peace to the Angel race, and all who dared to come against her authority were destroyed under her sword.
However, when the creatures of the Void appeared and civilization was in shambles, she rose to the call. Leading the Moonlit Order, she faced the attack head-on.

Thankfully, she wasn’t the only one fighting. Along with the Order, they managed to purge the chaos, but at a great cost. The battle took too many lives, so when it all ended, she knew something had to be done.
That was when she stepped toward the Void in search of the Lunar Blade.
It was said before the disappearance of the Celestial Angel race, a mysterious sword appeared that was meant to be wielded by the one meant to bring the angel race to peace and prosperity.
Legend has it that she never returned for millions of years, causing her name to fade from all minds and her legacy to slowly corrode.
However, when the Void opened again and the creatures from within came, legend has it that on that fateful day, Selphira Lunaris was born.
...not as the leader of the Moonlit Order, but as Selphira Lunaris, the wielder of the Lunar Eclipse Sword and the dancer whose movements alone are enough to mesmerize those she faces.
It was said that before the disappearance of the Celestial Angel race, the fracture that appeared in the nine Angel races ran deeper than one would have expected.
The fracture went as far as affecting the celestial constellation, one that made only one alignment possible. After that alignment, none would ever grace the Angel race again.
That alignment was what birth Selphira Lunaris.
However, Kent and his women stood and stared at the sky, watching the alignment of the Celestial Star and the Harmonious Moon, which had been dimmed for billions of years already.
Far in the cosmos, every Angel race was on their knees, singing the rebirth of the Lunar Child, the one said to usher the Angel race into a new age.
Those who believed in the Lunar Child were kneeling, prostrating themselves before her name.
Kent looked up at the sky, and a smile appeared on his face.
"When all hope was lost... when races were in shambles, she rose from the moon’s radiance, blessed by both the Celestial Mother and the Lunar Warden.

Her name spread far and wide, and wielding the moon’s power and the authority of the celestial star, she brought order to the Universe. Her name was once Seraphina Moonveil, but she became Selphira Lunaris.
...Once again, her name shall be Selphira Lunaris, the Celestial Sword Dancer."
"Rise and heed thy call, Selphira Lunaris, your destiny awaits."
When Kent invoked her true name, the sky turned even brighter, causing everyone to shield their eyes. The brilliance of the light was just too much to be seen with normal eyesight.
However, the light receded after a few minutes. That was when she appeared, dressed in white with golden embroidery lining the edges.

She had white hair with touches of silver here and there. She had the perfect warrior posture, and just like her sisters, her chest and backside didn’t betray her. In her hand was a longsword glowing with lunar energy.
Purple gems were embedded in the hilt of the sword. Her eyes were purple, shining with otherworldly brilliance.
On her back were three pairs of whitish-silver angelic wings.
"Wow, she is gorgeous," Vexthra said, watching their sister fly toward Kent and then jump into his arms, kissing his lips. The whole sight looked dreamy.
However, she could not be ignored since her nature had now changed from human to angel.
"How do you feel?" Kent asked after breaking the kiss. He always asked the same of all his ladies after their true name was awakened.
"I feel like the best version of myself," Mara giggled, looking at her sister. The two were stark contrasts when it came to race.
Nara was a Duskwraith Kin, meaning she was Half-Wraith, Half-Human, while Mara was an angel from the Moonlit Angel race.
One was of darkness, and the other was made of light, like yin and yang.

"I have also reached the peak of the Core Formation stage. The only thing left is to evolve my core seven times, so be ready to go on for days after all of this is over," Kent smiled, hearing her words.
Mara’s bloodline had already awakened to 25% so that she could wield her powers to some extent. Her form was also the same; she could hide her wings.
Aside from that, her beauty remained the same, striking and mesmerizing.
Zaila, who had brought out her Primordial spirit, stared at this wide-eyed. Her Primordial spirit seemed even more shocked by the changes that happened to Mara.
Her nature had basically changed from human to angel, and now, even if she were to face a Peak Core Formation expert who had evolved their core three to four times, she wouldn’t panic.
"Congratulations on your breakthrough," Kent said, smiling. "You should focus more on understanding your new powers. I have a feeling you will discover something interesting."
He turned to Camilla, who was smiling with Mara.
"Camilla dear, it’s your turn."
She walked forward, and just like with Mara, Kent put her blood and his blood on the token. And just like that, the second awakening of the day started.

Legend has it that she never returned for millions of years, causing her name to fade from all minds and her legacy to slowly corrode.
However, when the Void opened again and the creatures from within came, legend has it that on that fateful day, Selphira Lunaris was born.
...not as the leader of the Moonlit Order, but as Selphira Lunaris, the wielder of the Lunar Eclipse Sword and the dancer whose movements alone are enough to mesmerize those she faces.
It was said that before the disappearance of the Celestial Angel race, the fracture that appeared in the nine Angel races ran deeper than one would have expected.
The fracture went as far as affecting the celestial constellation, one that made only one alignment possible.
After that alignment, none would ever grace the Angel race again.
That alignment was what birth Selphira Lunaris.
However, Kent and his women stood and stared at the sky, watching the alignment of the Celestial Star and the Harmonious Moon, which had been dimmed for billions of years already.
Far in the cosmos, every Angel race was on their knees, singing the rebirth of the Lunar Child, the one said to usher the Angel race into a new age.
Those who believed in the Lunar Child were kneeling, prostrating themselves before her name.
Kent looked up at the sky, and a smile appeared on his face.
"When all hope was lost... when races were in shambles, she rose from the moon’s radiance, blessed by both the Celestial Mother and the Lunar Warden.
Her name spread far and wide, and wielding the moon’s power and the authority of the celestial star, she brought order to the Universe.
Her name was once Seraphina Moonveil, but she became Selphira Lunaris.
...Once again, her name shall be Selphira Lunaris, the Celestial Sword Dancer."
"Rise and heed thy call, Selphira Lunaris, your destiny awaits."
When Kent invoked her true name, the sky turned even brighter, causing everyone to shield their eyes.
The brilliance of the light was just too much to be seen with normal eyesight.
However, the light receded after a few minutes.
That was when she appeared, dressed in white with golden embroidery lining the edges.
She had white hair with touches of silver here and there.
She had the perfect warrior posture, and just like her sisters, her chest and backside didn’t betray her.
In her hand was a longsword glowing with lunar energy.
Purple gems were embedded in the hilt of the sword.
Her eyes were purple, shining with otherworldly brilliance.
On her back were three pairs of whitish-silver angelic wings.
"Wow, she is gorgeous," Vexthra said, watching their sister fly toward Kent and then jump into his arms, kissing his lips.
The whole sight looked dreamy.
However, she could not be ignored since her nature had now changed from human to angel.
"How do you feel?" Kent asked after breaking the kiss.
He always asked the same of all his ladies after their true name was awakened.
"I feel like the best version of myself," Mara giggled, looking at her sister.
The two were stark contrasts when it came to race.
Nara was a Duskwraith Kin, meaning she was Half-Wraith, Half-Human, while Mara was an angel from the Moonlit Angel race.
One was of darkness, and the other was made of light, like yin and yang.
"I have also reached the peak of the Core Formation stage.
The only thing left is to evolve my core seven times, so be ready to go on for days after all of this is over," Kent smiled, hearing her words.
Mara’s bloodline had already awakened to 25% so that she could wield her powers to some extent.
Her form was also the same; she could hide her wings.
Aside from that, her beauty remained the same, striking and mesmerizing.
Zaila, who had brought out her Primordial spirit, stared at this wide-eyed.
Her Primordial spirit seemed even more shocked by the changes that happened to Mara.
Her nature had basically changed from human to angel, and now, even if she were to face a Peak Core Formation expert who had evolved their core three to four times, she wouldn’t panic.
"Congratulations on your breakthrough," Kent said, smiling.
"You should focus more on understanding your new powers.
I have a feeling you will discover something interesting."
He turned to Camilla, who was smiling with Mara.
"Camilla dear, it’s your turn."
She walked forward, and just like with Mara, Kent put her blood and his blood on the token.
And just like that, the second awakening of the day started.

chapters.title: Chapter 567: Astraelynn, the Spear of Dawn
paragraphs: Before everything, you must first learn of the infamous Spear of the Dawnsters, the first and only spear forged at the heart of the Dawnstar.
A Celestial spear that could pierce the darkness and reveal all hidden dangers. Its nature was to destroy the darkness and bring light to the world.
This spear was first wielded by a legendary warrior known as Elyndra Kaelith. She existed during ancient times when the cosmos was very young.
She was an Aurielian — a race born from the starlight itself, blessed with beauty, grace, and powers drawn from the pure energy of dawn.
Legend has it that though the Aurielians are powerful, during dawn, they can be considered immortals, for no weapon in existence could kill them.
Elyndra Kaelith was the sole wielder of the Spear of Dawn - Luminis.
She led her people through thick and thin.

When the shadow forces appeared and threatened to cover the entire world in darkness, Elyndra Kaelith wielded this spear and, using the light, vanquished the shadow forces to the outer reaches of time, where she sealed them at the cost of her mortal form.
However, due to her dedication and incredible might she had shown, when she died, her soul was bound to the Spear of Dawn and set to await its next wielder.
Millions of years passed until Serelya Kaelith was born.
During her time, the shadow force that was sealed away started to break free. The seal holding them was weakening, and the forces on the outside who sought to free them were drawing closer.
Serelya Kaelith was a prodigy from a young age. She was known to wield both the power of the wind and light.
Unfortunately for her, during her era, there was war everywhere, and her race, which once led the charge against the shadow force, was now reduced to a pitiful state.
The Spear of Dawn that had once been used by Elyndra Kaelith had been asleep for millions of years.
Years passed, and the Spear never chose even those with the purest form of the Aurielian bloodline and impeccable battle prowess.
And so, when the force of the shadow was finally unleashed upon the world, there was chaos everywhere.

Many perished, and despite it all, the Spear remained asleep until the day Serelya Kaelith appeared in front of the Dawn Temple and cried her tears of anguish, cursing the very Spear that was meant to be used to protect all.

Having lost everything, he felt sorrow and anger bottled up to the point that when she finished letting everything out, the temple shook, and the one dominant spear that had been asleep for millions of years awoke.
That day, light shone upon the world again.
The darkness that had covered the entire world was destroyed by the light. But all of this happened at the cost of Serelya Kaelith’s life.
Like her ancestor Elyndra Kaelith, she lost her mortal body and was bound to the Spear of Dawn, going to sleep yet again.
Many years later, when the Creatures of the Void came, it had to wake up again. This time, the one it picked was a young warrior named Lynn.
She was left to die on the battlefield, but during her last moments, the Spear of Dawn arrived and saved her.
This time, instead of taking, it gave. It gave life to its wielder, and that was the day Astraelynn, the one known as the Spear of Dawn, was born.
With the power of light and great determination, the legacy of Astraelynn, the Spear of Dawn, spread everywhere.
The Creatures of the Void came, but she marched into battle using her spear, and to this day, her legend is spoken of on every battlefield.
For when the Spear of Dawn appeared on the battlefield, she was followed by an undying light.
Camilla hovered in the air, surrounded by a brilliant light that caused everyone except Kent to watch what was happening.
Camilla was being transformed into her true form. Surrounding her were three identical copies of her, each a beauty to behold.
They seemed to be whispering the secret of the dawn to her, or perhaps, they were telling her about the legacy she had now taken on as the Spear of Dawn.

Either way, after they were done whispering, they transformed into a magnificent spear that hovered before Camilla. When her hand touched it, lightning echoed through the cloud, spreading through the soul.
Then she was enveloped in a brilliant light. That was when Kent started to speak, and the white light containing Camilla entered the clouds.

"The first was the mother, who wielded the Spear of Dawn and guided the light to drive away the darkness. Then came the daughter, who, using her pain and anger, commanded the light to vanquish her foes.

At last, the tether that was meant to tie it all came, undying even at her last breath. She wielded her legacy and, after awakening her destiny, she tied it all and named it Astraelynn, the Spear of Dawn.
Today, we bear witness to the awakening of the Spear of Dawn. The one that will bring light into the world again...
... Rise, Astraelynn, the Spear of Dawn, your destiny awaits."
The heavens acknowledged her call, as a white pegasus came from the clouds, carrying on her back the Spear of Dawn, Astraelynn.
She was clad in a white celestial gown fashioned into elegant armor. Her beautiful white hair was styled with a delicate golden braided circlet.
Considering she is an Aurielian, a race of women blessed with beauty, her high cheekbones and large, expressive violet eyes framed her beauty quite well.
In her hand is a golden spear... the Spear of Dawn, holding the power of light and justice. She moved across the beautiful sky for a few minutes before she landed.
The moment she got down from the back of the Pegasus, it melded into her spear, vanishing from sight.
"I know this spear; it’s the Spear of Dawn, one of the celestial relics," Vexthra suddenly said, feeling a headache coming on.
"I don’t know which of the celestials think this belongs to them, but it’s now mine. They can cry tears of anguish all they want," Camilla said, spinning the spear around.
Vexthra could only smile and shake her head, watching this.
"To think someone that something even we gods weren’t allowed to stand 10,000 miles close to is now being spun casually by a mortal... Ah, who am I kidding? Nothing about this guy is normal."
Kent smile, "Like Cami said, they can cry to their mommies."
Vexthra only smiled and wondered what was happening now at the celestial realm, specifically at the palace where the Supreme Celestial resides.

chapters.title: Chapter 568: Astraethryn, the Weaver of Eternal Grids
paragraphs: Long ago, in the far reaches of the celestial realms, a cosmic event descended on all, causing the stars to align in a rare phenomenon known as the Trine of Eternity.
It was a convergence of three ancient astral bodies whose energies intertwined perfectly.
This event occurred once every ten thousand years and was believed to be the time when the veil between realms thinned, allowing cosmic power to pour freely into the world.

From the heart of this celestial alignment, the Varathyn Bloodline—a revered lineage of Celestial Weavers—channeled the cosmic energies to weave the very fabric of magical grids that sustained the balance between dimensions.
The bloodline was born of stars and space, with ancestors who had forged indestructible seals to imprison chaos entities and preserve peace across universes.
They were known as the first weavers who touched the secrets of reality and runes, granting them impeccable control over the weave of space and stars.
They were known far and wide as the progenitors of formations, arrays, and runes.
They stood at the forefront of every major war, and due to their brilliance and dedication, they imprisoned countless world-shattering entities.
Due to their dedication, they received the prophecy foretelling the birth of the supreme Weaver, and for millions of years, they waited for the fated birth.
Millions of years later, Selene Varathyn was born in those chaotic moments when the creatures of the Void came. Her birth occurred on a battlefield where her mother was breathing her last breath.
However, despite the unfortunate circumstances of her birth, Selene Varathyn crafted her first Celestial Grid when she was just ten.
It was a powerful protective formation that sealed away a rampaging spirit that had threatened the Celestial Weaver sanctum, where she was studying.
This feat earned her the title "Arcane Formation Prodigy" among the clans.

But that was just the beginning for her. It was said that at the peak of the battle against the creatures of the Void, she crafted millions of defensive, attacking, enhancement, and various other formations that saved countless lives.
Legend even had it that she single-handedly barricaded an entire galaxy in with a defensive and offensive formation, and for 366 days, no creature of the Void could penetrate it.
The forbidden legends spoke of the time her feat in battle impressed the Soul Weaver, earning her a visit that changed her perspective on everything.
This led her to create the Eternal Grid Codex, the tome said to contain forbidden formations and weaves, influenced by the Soul Weaver.
For years, her Grids protected life and fought against evil.
However, when the Voidborn Legion performed the Ritual of Eternal Doom, unleashing one of the five, the Ancient Void Elders, she was forced to do the impossible.

Legend has it that when the Void opened one last time, bringing one of the five horrors of the Void, Selene Varathyn drew her final grid, The Eternal Love Grid, one that trapped the Void Elder, sealing away the Void for who knows how long.
However, to do that, she had to burn her own soul. This act touched the universe, and in her last moment, she earned the True Name, Astraethryn, the Weaver of Eternal Grids.
Now hovering in the air is Alina, the one said to hold the legacy of Astraethryn, the Weaver of Eternal Grids.
Before her is a large codex flipping through its pages, using the knowledge inside to forge her body. She is being reborn from the wisdom of the Eternal Grid Codex.
Inside the Mountain Garden, Dori and Gaia looked at Akira with raised eyebrows.
⟪What? Why look at me like I have created an abomination?⟫ Akira asked with a smile.
⟪I mean, you didn’t create an abomination. However, you had to see her and even gave her that forbidden secret. Was mother aware?⟫ Gaia asked.
⟪And you think I went there on my own accord?⟫ Akira smirked.
⟪It was my mother who made me go. But even if she didn’t, I would have gone anyway. In our existence, we believed we were the only Weavers, and I mean, we are.
However, I saw what she could do, and despite us sitting at the peak, I was impressed. So I gave her the Forbidden knowledge and maybe a...⟫
⟪A what...?⟫ Gaia asked.
⟪Her blood essence.⟫ Dori, however, connected the dots. This made Gaia frown...
⟪You don’t think that was why...⟫ She wanted to say something, but Dori stopped her.
⟪It’s better not to say anything. The deed has already been done, and now, she has a disciple she must ensure grows into the Weaver she was meant to be.
Do I make myself clear, Akira?⟫ Dori wasn’t joking.
⟪I understand. I will take care of her.⟫ Akira wasn’t angry or anything.
However, a cardinal rule among the entities that came with the universe was that their bloodline could not be given to anyone, not even each other.
According to the rules, Selene Varathyn was to be banished since Akira enhanced her bloodline with her own. However, an exception was made for her, and she was allowed to live.
But...
Kent watched as the codex flipped to the last page. That was when the clouds parted, and strings of weaves descended on Alina until she was enclosed in a loop of runic strings.
A few minutes later, a large portrait of a serene garden featuring different types of things, which included birds, people, and beasts, appeared behind the loop cocoon.
It opened as long as 300 meters horizontally and 3 meters vertically.
"Oh my freaking god, this is the Celestial Portrait of the Eternal Garden!" Vexthra said, her expression shocked.
Kent turned and looked at her with a smile playing on his lips. "Let me guess, the Supreme Celestial will be screaming his head off by now."
"I fear there will be great panic in the God, Supreme, and Celestial worlds. It’s good I’m not around," Vexthra smiled weakly. Kent and her sisters laughed, knowing what she said was probably true.
At the same time, after opening for a few seconds, the portrait closed and shrank, turning into a scroll, then went into Alina’s forehead.
She snapped her eyes open, causing strings of weaves to form around her.
They formed into a staircase featuring 40 golden steps. She raised her hand and beckoned Kent to walk toward her.
Of course, the brat didn’t wait a second. He moved and stepped on the first step. However, he felt something enter his body when he stepped on the first step.
"Don’t stop, keep climbing," Alina said with a smile.

chapters.title: Chapter 569: Eternal Draconic Jade Body [Bonus]
paragraphs: Kent moved on to the second step, and when he did, he again felt something enter his body. He didn’t know what it was, but he felt no discomfort, so he stepped onto the third step.
Again, something entered his body, but looking at the 37 more steps to climb, he didn’t pay attention to this and instead focused on climbing.
Thankfully, there was no pressure, just the constant presence he felt entering his body. But as someone who trusted his ladies, he let them flow into him.
However, messages appeared in his vision when he stepped on the 10th step, making him pause for a second to read.
⟪You have absorbed the Eternal Jade Body Weave (1/4)⟫
⟪Your Primordial Draconic Body is reacting to the Eternal Jade Body⟫
⟪Your Primordial Draconic Body has merged with the Eternal Jade Body⟫
⟪Keep climbing to activate the mutated body. Progress: 25%⟫
Kent was visibly shocked. However, he didn’t stop and continued to climb even higher. When he reached the 20th step, a new message showing his progress appeared.
⟪Progress: 50%⟫
Inside the mountain garden, the three lolis were looking at what was going on inside the soul tower with clearly shocked eyes.
⟪Who would have thought something the Supreme Celestial has been after for billions of years is being given to Master on a silver platter?⟫ Gaia said with a chuckle.
Her sisters also laughed.
⟪This is just too much. They not only took the Spear of Dawn from him, but they even took the Celestial Portrait of the Eternal Garden from him? He must be pissed off by now.⟫
Akira also said, maintaining the same smile as her sisters.
⟪Whose fault is that? None of those things belong to him anyway, so he can just shut up and accept his loss.
I mean, putting such powerful items on display to show how powerful you are—no wonder the creatures of the Void and the others don’t take him seriously.⟫
Dori clearly didn’t like the guy, and while she made it look like she was on her master’s side, her sisters knew something else was at play here.
However, they didn’t dig into it...
⟪I wonder how powerful the master would become after this mutation?⟫ Just like Kent’s women were doing, the three of them also went back to staring.
After a while, Kent reached the 39th step, and Alina opened her arms, allowing him to come in the moment he stepped on the 40th.
A few seconds later, Kent took the last step, and a new message appeared. However, he first hugged the busty woman, her beauty shining like morning light.
The Alina standing before Kent was perfect in all aspects. She was damn beautiful. Her hair was a mix of red and brown tones, with a warm, slightly coppery glow and perfect bone structure.
Her body was shaped like an hourglass, and those hips were to die for.
Though all her sisters came out perfect in the chest and ass, Alina was on another level, one that made even her goddess sister jealous even before she met her.
Now, Kent could only wonder how they would feel, especially when they saw her naked.
Kent grabbed onto that ass and didn’t let go for a few minutes while he kissed her. Afterwards, he smiled at her, and the two flew down, causing the stairway to vanish.
Her sisters approached and started asking loads of questions.
This gave Kent the time to see what had changed about him, considering he felt his body change, and the feeling wasn’t something he could describe.
⟪Primordial Draconic Body ↠ Eternal Draconic Jade Body⟫
⟦Name: Eternal Draconic Jade Body⟧
⟦Grade: Unknown⟧
⟦Quality: Eternal⟧
⟦Description: A legendary body mutated from the infamous Primordial Draconic Body and the Unknown Eternal Jade Body.
The owner of this body gains flesh and spirit with the essence of ancient draconic jade, granting unparalleled resilience and longevity.
The jade’s eternal aura hardens the body to an indestructible state, capable of withstanding devastating blows and harsh environments.⟧
’Hold on a minute, my body is now indestructible. Does it mean I am immune to physical damage?’ Kent asked, feeling very happy.
However, his smile vanished the next second when Gaia spoke into his head.
⟪The master is not immune to physical damage. If a god strikes you right now, you will die. However, that doesn’t mean this new body mutation doesn’t have its advantages.
Before this, your Primordial Draconic Body could handle even a full-on attack from those three realms above you.
And let me tell you, taking on attacks from three realms is something even gods would be jealous of.
However, depending on the attacker, your body is now strong enough to handle four realms, even going as far as five.
However, that isn’t all. Because you are a body cultivator, the moment you reach the Diamond body, your Eternal Draconic Jade body will also improve significantly.
This will push your physical damage immunity to another level.
Every single rise in body cultivation is a huge leap in immunity against physical attacks. But that isn’t all.
...You are a dragon, you have a dragon bloodline. This means whenever your bloodline rises, your Eternal Draconic Jade Body will also increase with it.
Then there is the case of breaking a limit on your body. The moment the second limit is broken, you will understand just how powerful your new body is.⟫
’Slow down a little. I know you are excited, but care to tell me how much of a leap I will take after I break a limit, improve my bloodline to say 12%, and become a diamond body?’
Kent knew it was ridiculous to ask, but he had to ask, knowing the answer would tell him what to do next.
⟪Let’s forget about the other things. Currently, you can take on an attack from a Spirit King, someone four realms above you.

However, with a single leap in even your bloodline, or becoming a diamond body, your resistance to physical damage will prevent you from dying from an attack from a Spirit Emperor or even a Spirit Monarch.
Though that is not an invitation to go taunt them. The chances of you surviving a direct attack from a Spirit Lord are very high.
However, that doesn’t mean you should just stand there and let a Core formation expert bombard you with attacks. Trust me, you will die before you know how it happened.⟫
Kent smiled and then turned toward the beautiful Alina to reward her with more kisses.

"Alina, dear, what are you doing?" Kent asked.
"I am breaking the curse on her bloodline."
"Say what now?"
